title: Owner added to a Microsoft Entra application or service principal
description: Detects a successful Microsoft Entra audit operation that adds an owner to an application registration or enterprise application service principal.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary or unauthorized administrator may add an owner to an application or service principal to gain durable control over the identity object.
hypothesis.rationale: Application and service-principal owners can manage sensitive object configuration, credentials and permissions; Microsoft recommends monitoring ownership changes, although approved administrative transfers and application onboarding create legitimate events.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify successful owner additions to applications and service principals while leaving failures, removals, unrelated object types and incomplete events unmatched.

triage.summary: Establish the added owner, affected application object, initiating actor and business authorization, then review credential and permission changes.
steps: Review the initiating user or application, added owner, target application or service principal, source IP and correlation identifier.
Confirm the ownership change against an approved application-onboarding, support, migration or responsibility-transfer record.
Inspect subsequent credential, permission, redirect URI and consent changes; remove the owner and contain involved identities if unauthorized.
false_positives: Approved application onboarding, ownership transfer, support delegation and migration performed by authorized administrators

validation.expected_outcome: Match successful owner additions to applications or service principals; do not match failures, removals, other object types or events without a result.
